newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to supply oil to planned German refinery.
newsitem.headline: Russia to supply oil to planned German refinery.

text.p: The Russian government has approved a plan by state oil firm Rosneft and Megionneftegaz, a unit of Slavneft, to export up to 10 million tonnes of crude oil a year to 2010 to a planned oil refinery in Leuna, Germany.

The export project, detailed in a government decree published late on Tuesday and signed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, will send the oil via the Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline and write the exported volumes into Transneft's quarterly export schedule.
The Leuna refinery project in eastern Germany groups major partners Rosneft and Elf Aquitaine of France, with the Russian side financing its stake with crude oil supplies.
The facility is scheduled for completion by the end of 1997.
Crude oil producer Megionneftegaz 0MFGS.RUO is the main operating unit of Russian-Belarussian joint venture Slavneft.
